text:
Maya Chen: FYI support just escalated a latency regression from customer NovaHealth. They say p95 for /v1/generate jumped ~2-3x after the 2026-02-28 runtime deploy. Anyone already looking?

Anika (Support): Customer report + traces uploaded: https://files.internal/novahealth/traces/1743287001 (redacted). Observed around 2026-02-28T18:12Z. Throughput also drops on bursty traffic.

DeployBot: rollout/redwood-runtime/v2.14 completed to us-east-1 at 2026-02-28T18:05:12Z (canary 10% -> 100%). No automatic rollbacks triggered.

Sam Ortiz: @Maya thanks, pinging runtime/infra. Quick checks: 1) any node evictions? 2) kernel OOMs? 3) model-serving config changes?

Josh Patel: running a quick synthetic against redwood-2-7b in us-east-1 to reproduce. Command I'm using:
```bash
rbench --model redwood-2-7b --seq 2048 --concurrency 8 --rps 40 --duration 120
```
Will post numbers in 5m.

InfraBot: kube-node-eviction: node-gpu-12 evicted pods 2026-02-28T18:09:47Z; reason: DiskPressure.

Lena K.: DiskPressure on GPU nodes could explain tails if requests hit cold caches and compete with eviction/IO. Can we get `dmesg` and nv_peer_mem logs for node-gpu-12?

Sam Ortiz: Also check runtime config: we rolled in a change to batching/kvcache TTL in v2.14 — see PR #984: reduced KV cache expiry from 120s -> 30s to lower memory spikes. Could be more cache misses.

Josh Patel: rbench results (us-east-1, redwood-2-7b):
```
p50: 68ms
p95: 1.1s (expected ~450ms pre-deploy)
gpu_util: 46%
cpu_util: 38%
active_batches: 1-2 (no heavy batching)
error_rate: 0.1% (timeouts)
```
Seems p95 double-ish. Attaching raw client trace: https://files.internal/bench/1743287743

Anika (Support): customer traces show a pattern: lots of small requests (seq ~256) interleaved with occasional long ones (seq >1500). They call parallelized requests from a worker pool.

Maya Chen: @Lena @Sam can we reproduce with mixed workload? Maybe the kvcache TTL reduction causes more KV miss work for long sequences. Also DiskPressure + evictions could have caused some requests to land on nodes that just restarted.

Sam Ortiz: Good hypothesis. I'll run a mixed pattern that mimics NovaHealth: 10x short (256) + 1x long (2048) at concurrency 12. Command:
```bash
rbench --pattern "10x:256,1x:2048" --concurrency 12 --duration 180 --model redwood-2-7b --region us-east-1
```
Would appreciate a perf trace if someone can grab a flamegraph on those specific pods (pod names post in thread).

Josh Patel: Ran mixed workload; observed KV cache miss rate jump to 42% compared to 8% pre-deploy. Also saw increased serialized IO on node-gpu-12 right before an eviction. Snippet from runtime metrics around 18:08Z:
```
kv_cache_hit_rate: 58% -> 58% (oh wait)
kv_cache_miss_work_ms: 12ms -> 130ms
seq_processing_time_ms: p95 1100ms -> 2400ms for long seqs when cache miss
```
I think the miss_work path is doing more synchronous disk reads when cold.

InfraBot: kernel: [  1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, GPU hung. Recovered by reset. (node-gpu-12)

Lena K.: GPU hangs + DiskPressure is concerning. Could be a driver regression or flakey NVMe. Ops: schedule a pod drain for node-gpu-12 and repro on a clean node. Also roll back PR #984 on staging to confirm KV TTL impact.

Sam Ortiz: Agreed. Action plan:
1) Ops to cordon+drain node-gpu-12 and run rbench on a healthy node (assigned Josh).
2) Revert KV TTL change in a staging runtime and run mixed workload (assigned Sam).
3) Support to request extended customer traces and rate profiles (Anika).
4) If rollback reproduces improvement, prepare a hotfix rollback for prod canary (Maya/Lena).

Josh Patel: cordoned node-gpu-12 and scheduled test pods on node-gpu-18. Re-running mixed workload now.

(10m later)

Josh Patel: New results on node-gpu-18:
```
p50: 62ms
p95: 480ms
kv_cache_miss_work_ms: ~14ms
GPU resets: 0
```
Looks much closer to baseline.

Sam Ortiz: On staging, reverted PR #984 and ran identical mixed workload: p95 improved from ~1.2s -> ~510ms. KV miss work reduced.

Maya Chen: So root causes likely twofold: (1) KV TTL reduction increased cold-cache synchronous work causing latency for long seqs, (2) a flaky GPU node (disk/kernel issues) amplified the impact under bursty traffic.

Lena K.: Proposed mitigations for now:
- Roll back KV TTL change in prod canary (10%) and monitor for 30m.
- Mark node-gpu-12 for hardware investigation and move workloads off until fixed.
- Add short-term circuit: route long seqs to redwood-2-7b-8bit (lower mem path) when kv_cache_miss_work > 50ms. Example routing rule snippet:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
conditions:
  - header: x-seq-length
    op: ">="
    value: 1024
actions:
  - model: redwood-2-7b-8bit
```

Anika (Support): Notified NovaHealth about investigation and temporary routing plan. They asked for ETA — can we aim for rollback + monitoring within 1h?

Maya Chen: I'll coordinate rollback now. @DeployBot can you trigger a rollback of runtime v2.14 in us-east-1 to v2.13 for canary?

DeployBot: rollback requested: rollout/redwood-runtime -> v2.13 in us-east-1 (canary 10%). Started at 2026-02-28T18:56:04Z.

(20m later)

DeployBot: rollback completed to canary 10% at 2026-02-28T19:16:15Z. No failed pods reported.

Josh Patel: Post-rollback quickbench (canary nodes):
```
p50: 60ms
p95: 520ms
kv_cache_miss_work_ms: 16ms
```
Seems back to baseline on canary.

Sam Ortiz: Monitoring graphs show p95 for NovaHealth-like traffic dropping back to expected range on canary group. I'll watch for 30m and if stable we'll roll to 100% after signoff.

Maya Chen: Great work. Owners & follow-ups:
- Ops: investigate node-gpu-12 hardware (Lena)
- Runtime: prepare PR to make KV TTL change gated by autoscale/load (Sam/Josh)
- Support: confirm with NovaHealth and provide ETA (Anika)
- Deploys: plan safe rollout to 100% after 60m stable on canary (Maya/Deploy)

If anything new pops up please @channel. :thumbsup:
